routes.notes: landing page mentioning SSO + hints at /oauth2/token and /oauth2/authorize POST endpoints
with session cookie + form fields client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state — redirects to redirect_uri with ?code=<jwt>&state=<...>
with grant_type=authorization_code + client_id + redirect_uri + code — returns {token_type: 'Bearer', token: '<jwt>'}
requires Authorization: Bearer <jwt> where the JWT payload has type='admin'. Returns the flag if access is granted, otherwise 401.

observations: All JWTs are signed with HS256 using a single server-side secret.
POST /oauth2/token returns a Bearer JWT whose payload is base64-decodable without verification.
Login flow only ever sets ctx.session.type = 'user'; no admin login is exposed.
The /protected endpoint rejects any token whose decoded payload type is not exactly 'admin'.
